input.pql: PREDICT COUNT(orders.*, 0, 30, days) > 0 FOR EACH users.user_id

view.name: view_metric_from_source
view.yaml:
version: 0.1
source: "`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.orders"
filter: source.price > 50
joins:
  - name: users
    source: "`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.users"
    on: source.user_id = users.user_id
dimensions:
  - name: order_id
    expr: source.order_id
  - name: user_id
    expr: source.user_id
  - name: ts
    expr: source.ts
  - name: PRICE
    expr: source.price
  - name: price_band
    expr: CASE WHEN source.price > 100 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END
  - name: country
    expr: users.country
  - name: age
    expr: users.age
measures:
  - name: revenue
    expr: SUM(source.price)
  - name: buyers
    expr: COUNT(DISTINCT source.user_id)
  - name: average_price
    expr: AVG(source.price)

The view is created in the test schema from the yaml, its sources named with the {catalog} and {schema} placeholders the capture writes (no private name), each part backtick-quoted since Databricks reads a catalog's hyphen only quoted; its joins' on keys are bare, as people write them, so PyYAML reads each as the key true (KO3-40), which the reference reads too (DB/metric_view.py:825-909, join_cfg.get(True))
